pages.hook: In many American restaurants, the first thing a server does is bring water. Learn what to say about ice, time and the menu, so you feel relaxed at the table.

mythfact.s: In many American restaurants, the server brings you a glass of tap water for free.
mythfact.why: This is common: you can also say “No ice, please” if you do not want ice.

mythfact.s: You must order your food as soon as you sit down.
mythfact.why: You can say “Not yet, five more minutes.” Servers expect it.

mythfact.s: The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame is in Cleveland, Ohio.
mythfact.why: Yes, the museum opened in Cleveland in 1995.

mythfact.s: In the USA, a glass of water usually comes without ice.
mythfact.why: Ice water is the usual style, so people ask for “no ice” when they want it.

mythfact.s: “Mary Poppins” is a 1964 Disney musical film with Julie Andrews.
mythfact.why: Mary is a magic nanny who arrives in London with an umbrella.

lines: Ready to order? Wave to your server.

decode.q: What can you do if you need more time?

compare.br: In Brazil, the waiter often brings the menu and takes your drink order, and mineral water is often bought by the bottle.
compare.us: In the USA, the server often brings a glass of water first, then waits for you to be ready.
compare.tip: Say “Just water, please” and “No ice, please”. Both are polite and normal.
compare.ask: What do you drink with your meal? Say it in English.

quiz.q: You do not want ice in your water. You say…
quiz.why: No ice, please is short and polite.

quiz.q: You are not ready to order. You say…
quiz.why: Say it and the server will wait.

quiz.q: The server says “Enjoy your meal!” when…
opts: the food comes to the table
quiz.why: It is said when the food arrives.

Reading quest — Dinner in Cleveland · part 1
text: Tonight I am in **Cleveland** with my friend Pete. We want dinner. The restaurant is warm, and the room smells great.

A server named Maya comes to our table. She says, “Hi! **Can I get you something to drink?**” I say, “**Just water, please.**” She asks, “**With ice?**” “**No ice, please**,” I say. She brings the glass quickly. “**Here you go.** Ready to order?”

Pete and I are not ready. I say, “**Not yet. Five more minutes.**” Maya smiles. “**No problem. Take your time.**” We read the menu and look at the napkin, the fork and the spoon on the table. They are all ready, and so are we.

opts: A simple dinner in a restaurant
fast.why: The writer and Pete have dinner in Cleveland.

scan.q: What food does the writer have?

tf.s: The writer wants ice in the water.
tf.why: The writer says “No ice, please.”

tf.s: They need more time before ordering.
tf.why: “Not yet. Five more minutes.”

tf.s: Pete is the server.
tf.why: Maya is the server. Pete is a friend.

tf.s: Pete says “Cheers!”
tf.why: He lifts his glass and says Cheers.

order: The writer asks for water with no ice.
They ask for five more minutes.

ctx.sent: Take your time. We are not in a hurry.
ctx.why: In a hurry = needing to be fast.

ctx.sent: The soup is hot and delicious.
Would you like some more bread?

pages.think: What do you drink at dinner? Do you like ice in your drink?

pages.title: Reading quest — Dinner in Cleveland · part 2
text: Then the food comes. I have soup and a sandwich. It is hot and delicious! Pete has some bread. “Would you like some more?” he asks. “Yes, please!” I say. Pete smiles. “It reminds me of Mary Poppins: ‘A spoonful of sugar helps the medicine go down.’” We laugh.
Pete lifts his glass. “**Cheers!**” he says. “**Enjoy your meal**,” Maya says. I say, “Thank you!” Dinner is simple, but it is perfect.
